area: Reliability functionals for confidence signals: proper-scoring-rule decompositions (calibration vs discrimination/resolution), AUC vs ECE, rank-based robust association, empirical-Bayes/James-Stein shrinkage and Kelly-style fractional trust, selective prediction, and label-free estimators of channel reliability

methods.name: Murphy decomposition of the Brier score (reliability–resolution–uncertainty)
methods.key_idea: Any proper score splits into a calibration (reliability) term and a discrimination (resolution) term plus irreducible uncertainty; resolution is unchanged by monotone recalibration, so a signal can be maximally resolving while badly calibrated.
methods.relevance: The formal ground for the seed's central claim: the ECE gate fires on the reliability term while CISC's R1 success depends only on the resolution term. RTC should define reliability_hat as a resolution-type functional and report the decomposition on dev as a diagnostic.
methods.citation_hint: Murphy 1973, J. Applied Meteorology 12:595–600, 'A new vector partition of the probability score'; see also Sanders 1963; Bröcker 2009 QJRMS for the general proper-score version.

methods.name: DeGroot–Fienberg calibration vs refinement (sufficiency ordering)
methods.key_idea: Forecasters are compared by calibration and refinement; among calibrated forecasters, sufficiency/refinement is the decision-relevant ordering. A perfectly calibrated but unrefined forecaster is useless; an uncalibrated but refined one is valuable after recalibration.
methods.relevance: Second classical anchor for 'discrimination, not ECE'. Directly predicts the R1 failure of the binary ECE gate: under-confident-but-perfectly-ranked confidence is sufficient for the truth after a monotone map.
methods.citation_hint: DeGroot & Fienberg 1983, The Statistician 32:12–22, 'The comparison and evaluation of forecasters'.

methods.name: AUC / Mann–Whitney / Somers' D as monotone-invariant discrimination, with stratified (within-item) variants
methods.key_idea: AUC = P(confidence on a correct trace > on an incorrect trace) is invariant to any strictly monotone distortion of c; it equals a normalized Wilcoxon–Mann–Whitney statistic with known variance (DeLong; Hanley–McNeil). Somers' D = 2·AUC−1 gives a signed strength in [−1,1]. Pooling within-item comparisons is a stratified rank test (van Elteren).
methods.relevance: The primary candidate reliability functional: within-item Somers' D of c_i vs correctness, pooled across items, gives exactly the (sign, strength) sufficient statistic the seed wants, with a closed-form SE that feeds the shrinkage map. Note this matches CISC's own 'within-question' evaluation notion — cite, don't reinvent.
methods.citation_hint: Bamber 1975 J. Math. Psych.; Hanley & McNeil 1982 Radiology; DeLong et al. 1988 Biometrics; van Elteren 1960 (stratified Wilcoxon).

methods.name: Point-biserial and rank-biserial correlation; Fisher z for shrinkage-ready SEs
methods.key_idea: Point-biserial r is Pearson correlation of c with binary correctness (value-sensitive); rank-biserial r_rb = 2·AUC−1 is its monotone-invariant analog. Fisher z-transform gives approximately normal estimates with variance ≈ 1/(n−3), enabling clean empirical-Bayes shrinkage of the association estimate.
methods.relevance: r_rb is the natural estimand mirroring the simulator's kappa_c (the sim's c-model is linear-Gaussian in correctness, so r_pb ≈ kappa-driven). Recommend defining reliability_hat = shrunken rank-biserial, estimated within-item and pooled, so the monotone-distortion regime (ii) is handled by construction.
methods.citation_hint: Standard; Cureton 1956 Psychometrika for rank-biserial; Kerby 2014 for the simple-difference formula.

methods.name: ECE estimator pathologies (binning, adaptivity) and why gating on ECE is doubly wrong
methods.key_idea: Binned ECE is biased and binning-sensitive; adaptive/debiased variants exist, but even a perfect ECE measures only the calibration term — it is zero-information about ranking. Conversely low ECE can coexist with zero discrimination (predicting the base rate).
methods.relevance: Explains both failure directions of the prior binary gate: R1 (high ECE, perfect discrimination → wrongly shut) and the symmetric un-tested case (low ECE, useless signal → wrongly open). RTC should keep ECE only as a reported diagnostic, never as the gate variable.
methods.citation_hint: Naeini et al. 2015 AAAI (ECE); Nixon et al. 2019 CVPR-W (adaptive ECE); Kumar et al. 2019 NeurIPS (verified calibration); Gruber & Buettner 2022 NeurIPS (proper calibration errors) (verify last).

methods.name: Recalibration: Platt scaling / isotonic regression / logistic recalibration slope
methods.key_idea: A monotone map fitted on dev fixes calibration without changing AUC (isotonic) or with a parametric slope+intercept (Platt/logistic). A logistic recalibration with unconstrained slope also captures a NEGATIVE sign (anti-correlated confidence) — isotonic cannot flip sign.
methods.relevance: Crucial honesty point: the DEV-CALIBRATED RTC variant is very close to classic 'recalibrate on dev, then weight by recalibrated log-odds'. The recalibration slope IS a tempering exponent: logistic slope β on within-item z-scored c gives w_i = exp(β·z_i), β=0 → SC. Position RTC-dev as shrunk logistic recalibration + log-opinion pooling, which is a composition of known pieces.
methods.citation_hint: Platt 1999; Zadrozny & Elkan 2002 KDD; Niculescu-Mizil & Caruana 2005 ICML.

methods.name: Optimal weighted majority voting (Nitzan–Paroush) and plug-in weight consistency
methods.key_idea: For independent voters with competence p_i, the Bayes-optimal vote weight is log(p_i/(1−p_i)). With ESTIMATED competences, naive plug-in weights can underperform unweighted majority; finite-sample analyses give conditions and corrections (effectively shrinkage of estimated log-odds).
methods.relevance: Gives the 'full trust' anchor a principled form (CISC's c^gamma is a heuristic surrogate for log-odds weighting) and is the published proof-of-concept that estimated weights need tempering — the exact motivation for G2. Berend–Kontorovich-style bounds can calibrate how much dev data justifies how much gamma.
methods.citation_hint: Nitzan & Paroush 1982 Int. Econ. Rev.; Shapley & Grofman 1984; Berend & Kontorovich, 'Consistency of weighted majority votes', NeurIPS 2014 and JMLR 2015 (verify venue details).

methods.name: Generalized/fractional posteriors and SafeBayes learning-rate selection
methods.key_idea: Temper the likelihood/evidence by an exponent eta ∈ [0,1] to protect against model misspecification; eta=0 ignores evidence, eta=1 is full Bayes. SafeBayes (Grünwald) and information-matching (Holmes–Walker) LEARN eta from data; Bissiri–Holmes–Walker give the general belief-update framework.
methods.relevance: This is the closest existing formalization of 'continuous tempering with an estimated trust parameter' and supplies RTC's anchor-point structure (G4) for free: w_i = [odds(c_i)]^gamma is a fractional-posterior update per trace. Cite it; the LLM-voting application appears unclaimed, the mechanism is not.
methods.citation_hint: Grünwald 2012 ALT / Grünwald & van Ommen 2017 Bayesian Analysis (SafeBayes); Bissiri, Holmes & Walker 2016 JRSS-B; Holmes & Walker 2017 Biometrika; Wu & Martin 2023 survey on learning-rate selection (verify).

methods.name: James-Stein / empirical-Bayes shrinkage of an estimated association
methods.key_idea: Shrink a noisy estimate toward the null in proportion to its sampling variance: positive-part JS gives gamma_hat = r_hat·max(0, 1 − SE²/r_hat²) (or the EB posterior-mean under a normal prior on Fisher-z scale). Automatically → 0 as signal-to-noise → 0, continuous, no tuning.
methods.relevance: Provides the exact g(reliability_hat) mapping for G2/G4 with defensible defaults, replacing an arbitrary schedule. Precedent for shrinking WEIGHTS specifically: Ledoit–Wolf covariance shrinkage for portfolio weights; Efron–Morris for many-means. Recommend the LCB variant (shrink using a lower confidence bound) for the 'never below SC' claim.
methods.citation_hint: James & Stein 1961; Efron & Morris 1975 JASA; Efron 2010 'Large-Scale Inference'; Ledoit & Wolf 2004 J. Multivariate Anal.

methods.name: Kelly criterion and fractional Kelly under parameter uncertainty
methods.key_idea: Full Kelly maximizes log-growth given the TRUE edge; with an estimated edge, overbetting is catastrophically asymmetric (growth → ruin faster than underbetting loses growth), so the optimal stake under estimation error shrinks toward zero — fractional Kelly is EB shrinkage of the bet.
methods.relevance: The right way to frame why gamma_hat should be a shrunken/LCB estimate even when the point estimate says full trust: R5's 0.412 collapse is 'overbetting a mis-signed edge'. Motivation and asymmetric-loss argument, not a theorem to borrow verbatim.
methods.citation_hint: Kelly 1956 Bell Syst. Tech. J.; MacLean, Thorp & Ziemba 2011 (eds.), The Kelly Capital Growth Investment Criterion; Baker & McHale 2013, 'Optimal betting under parameter uncertainty' (verify).

methods.name: Selective prediction / reject option (risk–coverage analysis)
methods.key_idea: Chow's reject option and modern selective prediction use only the RANKING of a confidence score to trade coverage for risk; risk–coverage curves are the discrimination-only summary of a confidence signal.
methods.relevance: Independent support for rank-based usage; also suggests an additional evaluation view for the harness: per-regime risk–coverage curves of the confidence channel, which visualize discrimination collapse (R5 curve inverts) without any calibration confound.
methods.citation_hint: Chow 1970 IEEE Trans. IT; El-Yaniv & Wiener 2010 JMLR; Geifman & El-Yaniv 2017 NeurIPS.

methods.name: Dawid–Skene EM and spectral crowdsourcing (Karger–Oh–Shah; spectral+EM)
methods.key_idea: Estimate annotator confusion matrices from redundant unlabeled votes via EM; spectral/message-passing methods give provable initialization and minimax rates, all under conditional independence of annotators given truth.
methods.relevance: Canonical label-free reliability estimation, but the mapping to RTC is NOT 1:1: traces are exchangeable draws from ONE model (one 'annotator' = the confidence channel), so cross-annotator covariance identifiability is unavailable; identification must come from cross-item variation and vote margins. Still, D&S-EM treating each trace slot as an annotator is a required baseline (the seed already lists it).
methods.citation_hint: Dawid & Skene 1979 JRSS-C; Karger, Oh & Shah 2011 NeurIPS / 2014 Oper. Res.; Zhang, Chen, Zhou & Jordan 2016 JMLR 'Spectral methods meet EM'.

methods.name: Parisi–Strino–Nadler–Kluger spectral meta-learner (verified: PNAS 2014, arXiv 1303.3257)
methods.key_idea: Under conditional independence, the off-diagonal covariance of binary predictors is rank-one; the leading eigenvector recovers balanced accuracies UP TO A GLOBAL SIGN, resolved only by assuming most predictors beat chance.
methods.relevance: Proves the seed's suspicion: sign ambiguity is fundamental in label-free reliability estimation. The echo regime (majority confidently wrong) is exactly the case where the sign-fixing assumption fails — so the label-free RTC variant cannot be made assumption-free; state the identifiability condition explicitly rather than claiming unconditional G2.
methods.citation_hint: Parisi, Strino, Nadler & Kluger 2014 PNAS 111(4):1253–1258; follow-ups: Jaffe, Nadler & Kluger 2015 AISTATS; Platanios et al. 2014/2016 (estimating accuracy from unlabeled data).

methods.name: Disagreement/agreement as unsupervised accuracy: GDE and agreement-on-the-line (verified)
methods.key_idea: Disagreement rate between two independent runs on unlabeled data ≈ test error, provably WHEN the ensemble is class-wise calibrated (Jiang et al. ICLR 2022); agreement tracks accuracy linearly under distribution shift (Baek et al. 2022).
methods.relevance: The theoretical backbone for the agreement proxy (seed idea 2) AND its published failure condition: ensemble miscalibration (= correlated errors / echo clusters) is exactly when agreement-based reliability estimates break. Borrow their diagnostic: check calibration of vote-share vs majority-correctness on dev to certify the proxy before trusting the label-free sign estimate.
methods.citation_hint: Jiang, Nagarajan, Baek & Kolter 2022 ICLR, arXiv 2106.13799; Baek et al. 2022 NeurIPS 'Agreement-on-the-line'; caveat note: Kirsch & Gal 2022, arXiv 2202.01851.

methods.name: Learning with noisy labels applied to the agreement pseudo-label
methods.key_idea: Treat 1[a_i = majority] as a noisy proxy for correctness with item-level flip rate 1 − P(majority correct); with flip rate < 1/2 and an estimate of it (e.g., from vote margin via a calibrated margin→accuracy map), association estimates can be debiased with method-of-moments corrections.
methods.relevance: Turns 'the proxy is poisoned' into a quantitative bias correction: weight items by margin, estimate flip rate from dev or from margin distribution, debias the pooled Somers' D. This is the concrete mitigation path for seed idea 2 and should be specified with formulas in the deliverable.
methods.citation_hint: Natarajan et al. 2013 NeurIPS 'Learning with noisy labels'; Northcutt et al. 2021 JAIR 'Confident learning'; Donmez, Lebanon & Balasubramanian 2010 JMLR (unsupervised error estimation with known marginals); Steinhardt & Liang 2016 (unsupervised risk estimation).

methods.name: CISC — Confidence-Informed Self-Consistency (verified: Taubenfeld et al., arXiv 2502.06233, ACL Findings 2025)
methods.key_idea: Weighted majority vote with self-reported confidence; introduces WITHIN-QUESTION confidence evaluation and reports that the most CALIBRATED confidence method was the LEAST effective for weighting — i.e., the discrimination-vs-calibration point is already in this paper.
methods.relevance: Primary baseline and the paper RTC must be positioned against. RTC cannot claim novelty for 'discrimination not calibration' or for within-item evaluation; the open gap CISC leaves is fixed, non-adaptive trust (no gamma estimation, no anti-correlation robustness, no label-free reliability channel).

methods.name: DeepConf, RASC, ReASC, ESC/Adaptive-Consistency, Self-Calibration — the 2023–26 confidence-in-SC family (verified titles)
methods.key_idea: DeepConf (arXiv 2508.15260) filters/weights traces by local confidence online, label-free; RASC (arXiv 2408.17017, NAACL 2025) early-stops using answer consistency + rationale quality; ReASC (arXiv 2601.02970) aggregates by frequency+confidence for sample efficiency; ESC/Adaptive-Consistency (arXiv 2305.11860 etc.) stop on posterior stability; Self-Calibration (arXiv 2503.00031) distills SC-derived confidence back into the model then uses calibrated confidence for weighted SC/early stopping.
methods.relevance: The crowded neighborhood. All assume the confidence channel HELPS; none (per abstracts — verify full texts of ReASC and Self-Calibration before submission) estimate the reliability/sign of the channel or guarantee no-worse-than-SC under adversarial confidence. Self-Calibration is the closest in spirit to RTC-dev (recalibrate then weight) and must be a discussed baseline; ReASC's 'reliability' is evidence sufficiency, not channel trustworthiness.
methods.citation_hint: arXiv 2508.15260 (DeepConf); 2408.17017 (RASC); 2601.02970 (ReASC); 2305.11860 (Adaptive-Consistency); 2401.10480 ESC (verify id); 2503.00031 (Self-Calibration); DiVeRSe: Li et al. 2023 ACL (trained verifier weights, needs labels).

methods.name: LLM confidence quality literature (why per-deployment reliability estimation is needed)
methods.key_idea: Verbalized and token-probability confidences are systematically overconfident with model- and task-dependent monotone distortions; quality varies wildly across models/tasks (Kadavath 2022; Lin 2022; Tian 2023; Xiong 2024). Original SC paper already found raw-probability-weighted voting ≈ unweighted.
methods.relevance: Empirical case that (a) rank-based use is the right default under unknown monotone distortion, and (b) the association strength is a deployment-specific unknown — justifying estimating it rather than fixing gamma. Wang et al.'s null result for raw-weighting is a useful historical footnote for why value-based weighting is fragile.
methods.citation_hint: Kadavath et al. 2022 arXiv 2207.05221; Lin, Hilton & Evans 2022 TMLR; Tian et al. 2023 EMNLP 'Just Ask for Calibration'; Xiong et al. 2024 ICLR 'Can LLMs Express Their Uncertainty?'; Wang et al. 2023 ICLR (self-consistency, weighted variant in appendix).

novelty_assessment: Blunt verdict, piece by piece. (1) ALREADY PUBLISHED — the conceptual core: "discrimination, not calibration, is what makes confidence useful for weighting" is 50-year-old forecasting theory (Murphy 1973; DeGroot–Fienberg 1983) AND is already stated in the LLM-voting context by CISC itself (Taubenfeld et al. 2025 introduce within-question confidence evaluation and report the most-calibrated method was least effective for CISC — verified from the abstract). RTC cannot claim this insight; it can only operationalize it. (2) ALREADY PUBLISHED — tempering evidence by an estimated trust parameter: generalized/fractional posteriors with learned learning-rate (Grünwald's SafeBayes; Bissiri–Holmes–Walker; Holmes–Walker) is exactly "continuous tempering with data-driven eta, anchored at ignore-evidence and full-Bayes"; fractional Kelly and James–Stein plug-in-weight shrinkage (Berend–Kontorovich for weighted majority votes specifically) cover the shrink-under-estimation-error mechanism. The g(reliability)→gamma mapping is therefore an application of known machinery, and the paper should cite it as such. (3) ALREADY PUBLISHED — label-free reliability estimation in a NEARBY but not identical setting: Dawid–Skene/Karger–Oh–Shah/Parisi et al. PNAS 2014 estimate annotator reliabilities without labels, but require multiple conditionally independent predictors; our setting has ONE channel over exchangeable traces, so their covariance identification does not transfer — the honest statement is that crowdsourcing does NOT already solve our estimation problem, but it does prove the key negative result we inherit: the SIGN is identifiable only up to a better-than-chance assumption (Parisi et al.'s global sign ambiguity), which is precisely what echo regimes violate. Similarly, agreement-as-accuracy is published WITH its failure condition (Jiang et al. ICLR 2022: needs class-wise calibrated ensemble; Kirsch–Gal caveat note), which maps one-to-one onto the seed's "poisoned proxy" worry — cite rather than rediscover. (4) DIRECT COLLISION RISK in the 2025–26 SC literature: I found no paper that adaptively tempers the confidence exponent by an estimated reliability of the confidence channel or that handles anti-correlated confidence (kappa_c<0) — but the neighborhood is crowded and moving fast: ReASC (arXiv 2601.02970, 'Reliability-Aware Adaptive Self-Consistency') sounds like RTC but per its abstract 'reliability' means evidence sufficiency for stopping, not channel trustworthiness (READ THE FULL TEXT before claiming the gap); 'Efficient Test-Time Scaling via Self-Calibration' (arXiv 2503.00031) already does recalibrate-then-weight for SC, which overlaps heavily with RTC's dev-calibrated variant; DeepConf (2508.15260) is label-free confidence-weighted voting without a safety layer. (5) GENUINELY NOVEL, if executed: (a) the adversarial/anti-correlated axis itself — no SC paper I can find evaluates kappa_c<0 or provides a never-worse-than-SC guarantee; (b) the composite estimator: within-item rank-based signed discrimination (stratified Somers' D) + EB/LCB shrinkage to a tempering exponent with exact SC/CISC anchor points; (c) the label-free sign/strength estimator with margin-based debiasing and an explicit identifiability condition; (d) the falsifier-driven negative-control evaluation. Be honest in the paper that RTC-dev is essentially shrunk logistic recalibration + Nitzan–Paroush log-odds voting — a novel-in-context composition, not a new statistical idea — and that the label-free variant's core limitation (sign unidentifiability under correlated errors) is information-theoretic and inherited from Parisi et al., so G2 for the label-free variant must be scoped to regimes where the majority-better-than-chance condition holds or a minimal dev sign-check is allowed.
recommended_baselines: Plain SC (unweighted majority vote) — the G2 floor
CISC with gamma swept over {0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4} (per original paper), raw confidence
Rank-CISC: CISC on within-item rank/z-scored confidence with fixed gamma=1 — isolates the rank contribution from the tempering contribution
Binary ECE gate (the prior sibling method) — required for F3

Binary dev-AUC gate (gate on discrimination instead of calibration, threshold AUC>0.55 say) — the cheap fix to the prior method; RTC must beat THIS, not just the ECE strawman, or continuous tempering adds nothing
Dev-picked fixed gamma in {0,1} and dev-picked gamma on a grid — the F4 trivial baselines

Recalibrate-then-weight: logistic recalibration (unconstrained signed slope) of c on dev, then log-odds-weighted vote — the classic composition RTC-dev must be compared against and honestly related to
Oracle-tempered CISC: gamma tuned per-regime with ground truth — upper envelope
Dawid–Skene EM treating trace slots as annotators (label-free reliability baseline from crowdsourcing)
Parisi-style spectral/moment sign+strength estimate adapted to the single-channel setting (label-free)
DeepConf-style confidence filtering (top-eta% traces kept, majority vote) — modern label-free competitor
RASC-lite (already in harness) and an ESC/Adaptive-Consistency stopping baseline at matched token budget
Agreement-proxy RTC without debiasing (naive version) — needed to demonstrate the value of the margin-weighted/debiased estimator in echo regimes
risks: Sign unidentifiability is information-theoretic: with one confidence channel and exchangeable traces, no label-free method can distinguish 'confidence anti-correlated, majority right' from 'confidence correlated, majority wrong' in echo regimes (Parisi et al.'s global sign ambiguity). If the paper claims unconditional G2 for the label-free variant, a reviewer can construct a counterexample; scope the claim or require a minimal dev sign-check.

Collision with fast-moving 2025–26 literature: ReASC (2601.02970), Self-Calibration (2503.00031), DeepConf (2508.15260) each overlap with one component; only abstracts were checked here — full-text reads are mandatory before writing the novelty section, and results on at least one real LLM (not only the synthetic oracle harness) will be demanded, since all competitors report real-model results.

The simulator's confidence model is linear-Gaussian in kappa_c, which makes rank vs raw weighting nearly equivalent by construction; without the monotone-distortion regime (ii) the rank claim is untestable, and heterogeneous per-item kappa (regime i) can break any single global gamma — a scalar reliability functional is misspecified there and RTC may need to report this as a stated limitation.

Finite-sample noise in gamma_hat can violate F2 ('never significantly below SC') near kappa_c=0: a noisy positive gamma_hat on a small dev set occasionally overweights noise. Use the LCB/positive-part shrinkage and pre-register dev-set size and the shrinkage formula, otherwise F2 becomes a multiple-comparisons lottery across the sweep.

Budget frontier uses small per-item n (4–16 traces); within-item rank z-scores are extremely noisy at n=4 and ties/duplicate answers are common — specify tie handling (midranks) and consider pooling the calibration map across items rather than pure within-item ranking at small n.

RTC-dev may be empirically indistinguishable from the recalibrate-then-weight baseline (an F4-type outcome for the dev variant); if so the honest paper reports the dev variant as a repackaging and stakes novelty entirely on the label-free variant and the adversarial axis.

Kelly/James–Stein framing is motivation, not proof: no regret or dominance theorem is established for the voting setting; avoid stating G2 as a theorem unless proven under the simulator's generative model, and beware that the dev-AUC binary gate baseline may capture most of the practical benefit, leaving continuous tempering as a marginal refinement.
